title: FOR Loops & Arrays -- Scanning an I/O Bank
concept:
A FOR loop repeats a block a fixed number of times; arrays hold many values
under one name. Together they let you process a bank of I/O in a few lines:

    FOR i := 0 TO 7 DO
        Total := Total + Data[i];
    END_FOR;

Syntax: FOR i := start TO end [BY step] DO ... END_FOR;. The whole loop runs
inside ONE PLC scan, so keep counts sane -- a huge loop lengthens scan time.

Array indexing is Data[i]. In Studio 5000 arrays are 0-based (a DINT[8] has
indices 0..7), which is what we use here.
ab_note:
Studio 5000: arrays are 0-based, e.g. Data : DINT[8] -> Data[0]..Data[7]. FOR
loops are common for packing/unpacking status bits or scaling I/O banks. Watch
scan time on large iteration counts.
siemens_note:
SCL arrays can have arbitrary bounds, e.g. ARRAY[1..8] OF INT, so you'd write
FOR i := 1 TO 8. Same FOR ... END_FOR structure; just mind the index base. For
this exercise use 0..7 to match the data given.
task:
Given Data : an array of 8 integers (indices 0..7), compute two outputs with a
single FOR loop over i := 0 TO 7:

    - Total       : the sum of all Data[i]
    - Alarm_Count : how many Data[i] are greater than 100

Initialise Total and Alarm_Count to 0 before the loop.
starter:
(* Lesson 07 -- FOR Loops & Arrays: Scanning an I/O Bank *)

VAR
    Data        : ARRAY[0..7] OF INT;  (* 8-channel input bank, indices 0..7 *)
    i           : INT;                 (* loop index                         *)
    Total       : DINT;                (* output: running sum                *)
    Alarm_Count : DINT;                (* output: count of channels > 100    *)
END_VAR
